sports.h3: Sinner opens Montreal title defense after illness scare
sports.summary: Top ranked Jannik Sinner shook off a bout of tonsillitis to beat Borna Coric and launch his National Bank Open defense in Montreal.
body: Sinner returned from a short illness layoff to dispatch Borna Coric 6-2, 6-4 in the second round of the National Bank Open in Montreal. The world number one is defending the title he won last year and arrived without direct rivals Carlos Alcaraz and Novak Djokovic, both of whom skipped the Masters 1000 event.

The tournament runs August 2 to 13 with the men in Montreal and the women in Toronto. Second seed Alexander Zverev is the highest ranked player in the Montreal draw and Canadian hope Felix Auger-Aliassime is carrying home support deep into the week.

sports.h3: Zverev rolls in Montreal as seeds tumble
sports.summary: Alexander Zverev crushed Jordan Thompson for his tour leading 48th win of the year while Medvedev and Tsitsipas both crashed out early.
body: Second seed Zverev needed barely an hour to beat Jordan Thompson 6-1, 6-1 in Montreal, banking his 48th match win of the season and the most on the ATP Tour. The German looks a genuine threat in a draw thinned by absences at the top.

The upsets came fast underneath him. Alejandro Davidovich Fokina knocked out third seed Daniil Medvedev 6-4, 1-6, 6-2 and Kei Nishikori turned back the clock to beat eighth seed Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-4, 6-4.

sports.h3: Sabalenka and Swiatek open Toronto with No. 1 on the line
sports.summary: Top seed Aryna Sabalenka began her Toronto campaign against qualifier Moyuka Uchijima with the world number one ranking under threat from Elena Rybakina.
body: Sabalenka opened the night session in Toronto against Japanese qualifier Moyuka Uchijima, arriving with an 8,550 to 8,056 points lead over Elena Rybakina at the top of the rankings. A slip this week could hand the number one spot to her rival.
Iga Swiatek and Coco Gauff are also chasing the title in a stacked field that features 72 of the WTA top 75. Amanda Anisimova headlined the late slate against Thai qualifier Lanlana Tararudee.

sports.h3: Auger-Aliassime carries home hopes in Montreal
sports.summary: Felix Auger-Aliassime is the leading Canadian in a Montreal draw that could set up a quarterfinal against a recent Roland-Garros finalist.
body: With Sinner and Zverev anchoring the top half, Auger-Aliassime is Canada's best bet for a deep run on home soil. The draw projects a possible quarterfinal against a French Open finalist and a later collision with defending Masters names.
Ben Shelton and Daniil Medvedev had been penciled in as a possible quarterfinal, but Medvedev's early exit reshaped the bottom half and opened the door for others.

sports.h3: Spain make it two in a row at SailGP Portsmouth
sports.summary: Diego Botin steered Spain's Los Gallos to a second straight SailGP event win in Portsmouth, beating Sweden, Switzerland and Canada in the final.
body: Spain's Los Gallos claimed back to back SailGP victories at the Portsmouth Sail Grand Prix on July 25 and 26. Skipper Diego Botin led the crew past Artemis of Sweden, Switzerland's Explora and Canada's Northstar in a four boat final.

The result tightens the 2026 championship, which is being contested across thirteen grands prix worldwide. The fleet next races at the ROCKWOOL Germany Sail Grand Prix in Sassnitz on August 22 and 23.

sports.h3: Team USA joins swelling America's Cup field for Naples
sports.summary: American Racing confirmed its entry for the 2027 America's Cup after buying American Magic's AC75 and training boats as the fleet grows.
body: The Louis Vuitton 38th America's Cup will be sailed off Naples in the Italian summer of 2027 with the match starting July 10. Five founding teams from New Zealand, Britain, Italy, Switzerland and France have formed an alliance to shape the event's future.

American Racing, representing Sail Newport, confirmed its challenge after purchasing American Magic's key hardware including the AC75 Patriot and two AC40 platforms. A backed Australian challenge has also entered, filling out the road to Naples.

sports.h3: Norris wins dramatic Hungarian GP into summer break
sports.summary: Lando Norris held off Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli to win the Hungarian Grand Prix and take his first victory of his title defense.
body: Norris converted pole into victory at the Hungaroring on July 26 despite losing the early lead to Oscar Piastri, who retired with a gearbox failure. It was the first win of the reigning champion's title defense as the paddock headed into the summer shutdown.
Verstappen finished second ahead of Antonelli in third. Lewis Hamilton crossed fourth but a five second pit lane penalty dropped him to fifth and promoted Charles Leclerc to fourth.

sports.h3: Verstappen exit clause fuels summer silly season
sports.summary: With Max Verstappen outside the top two at the break, his Red Bull exit clause is in play and McLaren has emerged as a favored landing spot.
body: Verstappen sits seventh at the summer break, best of the rest behind Mercedes, Ferrari and McLaren with just two podiums all year. That leaves him below the top two threshold that reportedly unlocks an exit clause in his Red Bull contract.

Mercedes has long courted the Dutchman, but reports now cast McLaren as the frontrunner. Any move would trigger a grid wide domino effect, with Red Bull said to be eyeing Oscar Piastri if Verstappen departs.

sports.h3: Eredivisie kicks off Friday with PSV chasing four in a row
sports.summary: The 2026-27 Eredivisie season opens August 7 with Cambuur hosting Excelsior as three-time champions PSV and a rebuilt Ajax lead the title race.
body: The new Dutch top flight season begins the weekend of August 7 to 9, with SC Cambuur versus Excelsior Rotterdam as the curtain raiser and PSV facing Fortuna Sittard the next day. PSV go for a fourth straight crown.

Ajax are the biggest threat after signing Marcos Leonardo from Al-Hilal to boost their attack under coach Michel, with Davy Klaassen as captain. The full schedule is already set through matchweek 12 in November.

sports.h3: ADCC 2026 card shifts as champions pulled for UFC BJJ
sports.summary: The ADCC World Championship in Krakow lost multiple titleholders to the UFC's rival grappling series as the September event's lineup reshuffles.
body: The ADCC World Championship returns September 12 and 13 at Tauron Arena in Krakow, but the invite list keeps moving. Several past champions have been withdrawn, with the UFC BJJ series pulling contracted talent away from the biennial showcase.

The reshuffle has reopened brackets across weight classes and sparked debate over which grappling promotion holds the sport's top names. UFC BJJ 10 is set for August 20, adding to a crowded late summer calendar.

sports.h3: Craig Jones leaves CJI 3 on ice after cancellation
sports.summary: Craig Jones scrapped a third edition of his big money Craig Jones Invitational in May, and July talk of a return produced no confirmed event.
body: Jones confirmed in May that CJI 3 was cancelled, saying the economics no longer added up after the first two editions failed to turn a profit. CJI 2 broke even at best despite its headline million dollar purses.
By July there was renewed chatter about a scaled back return without the huge prize pool, but no venue, card or date has been verified. Jones has also said his event will not clash with ADCC in 2026.

sports.summary: The IBJJF Brazilian National Championship ran across ten days in Barueri near Sao Paulo with close to 8,000 competitors on the mats.
body: The IBJJF Brasileiro packed the Ginasio Poliesportivo Jose Correa in Barueri, part of greater Sao Paulo, with roughly 8,000 athletes over ten days of competition. It remains one of the largest gi tournaments on the calendar.
The federation's summer schedule stays busy, with international opens and the World Master championship lined up through August as the grappling season builds toward ADCC in September.

consumer-tech.h3: Tesla ships summer update as robotaxi push widens
consumer-tech.summary: Tesla's 2026.26 summer update is rolling out with a live self-driving indicator in the app, days after the company built its 10-millionth EV.
body: Tesla began pushing software update 2026.26 to vehicles worldwide, bundling new features, visual overhauls and usability fixes. A headline addition is a live app indicator showing when a car is actively driving itself, aimed squarely at owners who put vehicles into the expanding robotaxi fleet.

The rollout follows Tesla building its 10-millionth EV at the Fremont factory on August 2. FSD v14 Lite has gone to wide release and the company confirmed Starlink V5 integration in its Cybercab robotaxi vehicles, though critics note the robotaxi service is still scaling slowly.

consumer-tech.h3: Rivian pushes cheaper R2 trims back to 2027
consumer-tech.summary: CEO RJ Scaringe confirmed Rivian's more affordable R2 trims will slip to early 2027 as the company reported second quarter revenue of $1.66 billion.
body: Rivian retreated from a late 2026 target and now expects the lower priced R2 trims in early 2027. The line is running a single shift at roughly 600 units a week, with a second shift due by the end of the third quarter to nearly double output.

The company guided to 20,000 to 25,000 R2 deliveries this year and posted $1.66 billion in second quarter revenue as R2 shipments began. Management reaffirmed plans for point-to-point hands off driving by year end.

consumer-tech.h3: European EV sales jump as BYD keeps climbing
consumer-tech.summary: Battery electric sales across Europe leapt 50 percent to a 26 percent market share, with BYD's Atto 2 setting a registration record.
body: Fully electric car sales in Europe surged around 50 percent year over year to reach a 26 percent market share, according to the latest regional data. The growth reflects both new models and stronger charging confidence among buyers.

Chinese maker BYD kept gaining ground, with the Atto 2 posting a record 13,100 registrations in July on the back of a new plug-in hybrid variant. BYD is expanding its European sales network aggressively as it targets thousands of points of sale.

consumer-tech.h3: Tesla robotaxi rollout draws scrutiny over pace
consumer-tech.summary: Reports say Tesla's driverless robotaxi operation is expanding cautiously, with limited coverage and safety monitors still in the loop.
body: Even as Tesla touts autonomy milestones, analysts and reporters flagged that its robotaxi service remains small and heavily supervised. Coverage areas are limited and human oversight persists, tempering the company's marketing.

The new app indicator showing when a vehicle is driving itself is partly aimed at robotaxi owners who have a financial and safety stake in knowing their car's status. Tesla continues to frame the effort as its next major growth driver.

consumer-tech.h3: ChatGPT returns to WhatsApp across Europe
consumer-tech.summary: OpenAI brought ChatGPT back to WhatsApp in the European Economic Area with image, voice and multilingual chat plus optional account linking.
body: ChatGPT is available again on WhatsApp in the EEA, letting users message the verified 1-800-CHATGPT contact without an account. People can send text, upload images, share voice notes, generate images and chat in many languages, with account linking unlocking higher usage limits.
OpenAI also expanded its Sign in with ChatGPT beta across partner sites and tools including Airtable, GitLab, HubSpot, Notion, Supabase and Vercel, pushing its login into more third-party workflows.

consumer-tech.h3: Instagram adds built-in AI image generation
consumer-tech.summary: Instagram rolled out a first-party image model that lets users transform photos with preset styles or fully custom text prompts inside the app.
body: Instagram introduced its own image generation model, giving users a way to remix and transform photos using built-in presets or free-form prompts without leaving the app. The move brings generative editing directly into the main creation flow.
The feature lands as Meta pushes AI tools deeper across its apps, betting that in-app generation keeps creators from turning to standalone tools for edits and effects.

consumer-tech.h3: WhatsApp usernames near launch to hide phone numbers
consumer-tech.summary: WhatsApp is preparing usernames so people can message without exposing their phone numbers, alongside iPad registration and CarPlay upgrades.
body: WhatsApp is rolling toward a long requested usernames feature. Once live, users who opt in will no longer have to reveal their phone number when they first message a person or business, and can reserve a unique handle.
The update also brings direct account registration on iPads, a revamped Apple CarPlay and Android Auto experience, better PDF collaboration and music sharing through Status.

consumer-tech.h3: Android 17 spreads Gemini and focus tools
consumer-tech.summary: Android 17 is reaching more devices with Gemini integration, floating app Bubbles and a Pause Point screen for distracting apps.
body: Android 17 launched stable in June alongside the Pixel Drop and is now expanding to more phones. Highlights include deeper Gemini integration arriving this summer, Bubbles that turn any app into a floating window and Metric Style Live Update notifications.

A new Pause Point tool in Digital Wellbeing inserts a ten second pause screen before flagged distracting apps, offering a breathing exercise, a timer or a favorite photo. Advanced Protection also tightens accessibility and scam defenses.

consumer-tech.h3: Apple signals September event for iPhone 18 Pro
consumer-tech.summary: Reports point to a September 9 Apple event for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, with the standard iPhone 18 held back to spring 2027.
body: Apple is expected to hold its iPhone 18 Pro event around September 9, with pre-orders for the Pro and Pro Max plus new Apple Watches on September 11 and sales on September 18. The company is breaking from tradition by delaying the standard iPhone 18 to spring 2027.

The fall lineup is tipped to include Apple's first foldable, possibly branded iPhone Ultra, which could start at $2,000 or more. Analysts warn of $100 to $200 price hikes on the new Pro models tied to chip and camera costs.

consumer-tech.h3: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 goes on sale
consumer-tech.summary: Samsung's shorter wider Galaxy Z Fold 8 reaches general availability August 7 at $1,899, sitting below the new Z Fold 8 Ultra.
body: Unveiled at Unpacked in London in July, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 becomes broadly available August 7 starting at $1,899 for 256GB. It is a wider, shorter book style foldable aimed at first time buyers, with a 5.5 inch cover screen and a 7.6 inch inner display.
Samsung positioned it beneath the more premium Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra and alongside the Galaxy Z Flip 8, using new Flex Titanium construction for the main panel.

consumer-tech.h3: Google sets August 12 stage for Pixel 11
consumer-tech.summary: Google confirmed a Made by Google event on August 12 in New York for the Pixel 11 line, Pixel Watch 5 and a new 2nm Tensor G6 chip.
body: Google will unveil the Pixel 11 series at a Made by Google event on August 12 in New York, with retail availability starting August 20 and pre-orders opening on announcement day. The phones ship with Android 17 out of the box.
The lineup is expected to debut a 2nm Tensor G6 processor and a new Pixel Watch 5, with price increases anticipated across the range.

consumer-tech.h3: Garmin teases Fenix 8 reveal for late August
consumer-tech.summary: Garmin scheduled a virtual launch event for August 27 where the next Fenix flagship smartwatch is expected to headline.
body: Garmin is holding a virtual launch on August 27 that is widely expected to introduce a new Fenix flagship, which the company has teased as the future of its wearables. The event caps a busy 2026 for the brand.
Garmin has already expanded its entry level running lineup this year with the Forerunner 70 and Forerunner 170, broadening its appeal beyond hardcore athletes.

consumer-tech.h3: Bose targets Sonos with new Atmos soundbar
consumer-tech.summary: Bose launched the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar at $1,099 as a direct challenger to Sonos's flagship Arc Ultra in the Dolby Atmos market.
body: The Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar arrives as the company's new flagship Dolby Atmos bar, priced at $1,099 to match Sonos's Arc Ultra head to head. The launch sharpens competition at the top of the premium soundbar segment.

Rivals are crowding in too, with the WiiM Bar offering a custom eight driver array and up-firing speakers for immersive Atmos at a lower price. Sonos is expected to ramp its own hardware launches through the back half of its fiscal year.
